title: Customer Status Updates, Parts-Delay Holds and Courtesy Rides — Insurance Claim Repairs Service Standard
content:
Insurance Claim Repairs sets per class how often the customer hears about the repair and by which channel, how long a back-order may run before the repair order goes on hold for parts delay, how soon a hold is notified, and how far a courtesy ride reaches.

| Repair class | Most business days between status updates | Update channel | Back-order length beyond which a parts-delay hold begins (business days) | Notice to customer and insurer after a hold begins (business days) | Courtesy ride radius from the center (miles) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Express Claim Repair | 1 | text message (sms) | 2 | 1 | 10 |
| Standard Claim Repair | 2 | text message (sms) | 3 | 1 | 10 |
| Major Claim Repair | 2 | text message (sms) | 3 | 1 | 15 |
| Structural Claim Repair | 2 | phone | 5 | 1 | 15 |
| Certified Structural Claim Repair | 2 | phone | 5 | 1 | 15 |
| Aluminum Certified Structural Claim Repair | 2 | phone | 5 | 1 | 15 |

**Status updates.** The interval is the maximum number of business days between routine repair status updates to the customer; the channel is the one the class uses for those routine updates.

**Parts-delay hold.** The figure is a back-order length: a back-order longer than it puts the repair order on hold for parts delay. In Structural Claim Repair, with a figure of 5, a back-order of 5 business days does not exceed it and a back-order of 6 business days does.

**Hold notice.** In every class the customer and the insurer are notified within 1 business day after a hold begins.

**Courtesy ride.** A courtesy ride is offered at drop-off and pick-up within the stated distance from the center.
